title: Steplength selection in interior-point methods for quadratic programming
contribution: Replaces the common equal step length of primal-dual IPMs for convex QP by three multipliers (alpha_x, alpha_y, alpha_z) chosen to minimize a KKT-residual merit function over a set that contains all equal-step choices, solved by two 2-D QPs, and shows fewer iterations than equal steps and Meszaros's rule on the Maros-Meszaros set (pp. 4-8).
problem_entry: A literature-recommended conservative safeguard (equal step lengths under the fraction-to-the-boundary rule) is called unnecessarily conservative; eq. 2.8 shows why Q != 0 couples primal and dual steps and can make unequal steps diverge (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Minimize the merit function ||Ax-b||^2 + ||A^T y + z - Qx - c||^2 + x^T z over A1 (equal steps) union A2 (one bound pushed to its limit) with alpha_y free; inclusion of A1 makes it no worse than equal steps, and the subproblem is two 2-D bound-constrained QPs costing a handful of inner products (pp. 3-6).
assumptions: Convex QP in standard form, Q PSD, A full row rank, infeasible primal-dual IPM from (x,z) > 0 (p. 1); Meszaros characterization assumes conditions on r_p, r_d, Q dx 'normally achieved in practice' (p. 4); stop at KKT residual < 1e-6, max 200 iterations (p. 6).
proof_devices: residual-update algebra (2.8) and mu+(alpha) < mu for small common alpha, showing what equal steps guarantee (p. 3)
set inclusion A1 in A1 union A2, giving no-worse-than-equal-steps merit decrease by construction (p. 5)
Remark 4.1: reduction of the 3-variable step-length problem (4.15) to two 2-D bound-constrained QPs with explicit Q and c (pp. 5-6)
positive semidefiniteness of the A2 subproblem matrices, so that trial point solves a 2-D convex QP (p. 6)
global convergence asserted from merit decrease but not proved; no theorem in the paper (pp. 3, 6)
experiments: Matlab code, Maros-Meszaros convex QPs with AMPL models and < 10,000 variables (p. 6); three step-length rules in one code (eq., Meszaros, new), iteration counts only, Table 1 with 56 problems and relative differences, Dolan-More profile (pp. 6-7); Meszaros fails on qsierra as predicted (p. 6); new rule loses on qpcboei2 +25%, dual3 +22% without comment (p. 7); alpha_y = alpha_z ablation 'slightly less efficient', no numbers (p. 8).
positioning: Corrects the equal-step practice of IPM texts/codes [1,4,11] and the bi-objective rule of Meszaros [8], restated exactly via its efficient set before criticism; borrows unequal-step precedent from LP (Mehrotra) and NLP codes (Byrd-Hribar-Nocedal, Vanderbei-Shanno, Waechter-Biegler) and conjectures transfer to convex QP (pp. 2, 4).
writing: Eight-page letter; thesis in abstract and first intro paragraph; hedged ('We propose', 'We conjecture') yet asserts unproved global convergence (p. 3) and untested size-independence (p. 6); design reasons enumerated (p. 3); one-paragraph conclusion with no limitations (p. 8).
limits_future: No convergence proof despite the claim (p. 3); small problems only, iteration counts only (p. 6); losses in Table 1 not discussed (p. 7); ablation without numbers (p. 8); no future work stated (p. 8).

method_links.note: Early form: incumbent and rival rules implemented in one Matlab code with only the step-length rule varied, one-component ablation (alpha_y = alpha_z), rival failure printed and explained; but the incumbent's wins in Table 1 are not named in the text and no tuning disclosure.

Precursor: one merit function settles the infeasibility/complementarity trade-off inside each iteration, with the conservative equal-step choice kept as fallback set A1; no penalty/merit parameter update.
Weak: argues the rival's step criterion omits complementarity and justifies iteration counts by costing per-iteration work; the performance profile itself is not questioned.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The step-length search set A1 union A2 includes every equal-step choice, so the new rule decreases the merit function at least as much as the incumbent by inclusion, with no separate proof.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: predict the rival's failure, then show it
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Section 4 derives that Meszaros's rule can repeatedly choose (alpha_x, 0, 0) and stagnate; the experiments name qsierra, where it hits the 200-iteration limit for exactly this reason.

transferable: Relax a conservative rule by optimizing a merit function over a set that contains the conservative choice; the no-worse guarantee follows by inclusion (pp. 4-5).
Restrict the search set so the step-selection subproblem is a pair of 2-D bound-constrained QPs with explicit data, and cost it in inner products already computed elsewhere (pp. 5-6).
Give a rival an exact restatement (its efficient set) and a predicted failure mode before running it, then name the instance where the prediction comes true (pp. 4, 6).
Implement rival rules as interchangeable components of one code, vary only that component, and ablate the new degree of freedom (pp. 6, 8).
Report per-problem relative differences against the incumbent in one table next to a performance profile (pp. 6-7).

quotes.text: Empirical evidence has shown, however, that this approach is unnecessarily conservative in numerous cases.
This myopic choice may stagnate the algorithm as no step is taken in the dual space.
